summary_html:
The section formula finds the coordinates of a point \(P(x,y)\) that divides the line segment joining \(A(x_1,y_1)\) and \(B(x_2,y_2)\) in a given ratio \(m_1:m_2\). If the division is internal, the coordinates are \(x=\frac{m_2x_1+m_1x_2}{m_1+m_2}\) and \(y=\frac{m_2y_1+m_1y_2}{m_1+m_2}\). The formula follows from similar triangles: drawing perpendiculars from \(P\) to the axes creates two right‑angled triangles whose corresponding sides are proportional to \(m_1\) and \(m_2\). When \(m_1=m_2\), the point is the midpoint, giving \(x=\frac{x_1+x_2}{2}\) and \(y=\frac{y_1+y_2}{2}\).

As an illustration, a telephone company wants a relay tower \(P\) on the line AB such that \(PB\) is twice \(PA\). Taking \(A\) as the origin \((0,0)\) and \(B(36,15)\), the ratio \(PA:PB\) is \(1:2\). Substituting \(m_1=1, m_2=2\) into the section formula yields \(x=\frac{2\cdot0+1\cdot36}{1+2}=12\) and \(y=\frac{2\cdot0+1\cdot15}{1+2}=5\). Thus the tower is at \((12,5)\), exactly one‑third of the way from \(A\) to \(B\).

Another example asks for the points that trisect the segment joining \(A(2,-2)\) and \(B(-7,4)\). For the first trisection point \(P\), the ratio is \(1:2\); applying the formula gives \(P\bigl(\frac{2\cdot(-7)+1\cdot2}{3},\frac{2\cdot4+1\cdot(-2)}{3}\bigr)=(-1,0)\). The second point \(Q\) uses ratio \(2:1\) and yields \(Q(-4,2)\). These points are useful in dividing a line into equal parts for design or construction.

A frequent error is to mix up \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) in the numerator, which swaps the positions of \(A\) and \(B\) and places \(P\) on the opposite side of the segment. Always write the coordinate of \(A\) multiplied by the ratio attached to \(B\), and vice‑versa, as shown in the formula.

Beyond geometry, the section formula underlies interpolation in computer graphics, where a point between two known vertices is needed to draw smooth curves. It also appears in physics when locating the centre of mass of two particles placed at \(A\) and \(B\) with masses proportional to \(m_1\) and \(m_2\).
